heard: A four million sun black hole fits inside Mercury's orbit. This invisible monster sits at the heart of our Milky Way. Astronomers watch nearby stars whip around its gravity for decades. Eight radio telescopes then join to form a virtual Earth-sized eye. Dast orbits the whole so fast, its appearance changes every few minutes. Scientists say imaging it was like photographing a dog chasing its tail. Five years of supercomputer work finally revealed its glowing orange shadow. This massive anchor fits entirely inside the orbit of a single planet.
